newsitem.title: INDIA: India agrees to import wheat - government official.
newsitem.headline: India agrees to import wheat - government official.

text.p: The Indian government has agreed in principle to import wheat, but the quantities to be bought and the timing of any purchases have yet to be worked out, a government official said on Thursday.
"In principle a decision has been taken to import wheat," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters. "The time-frame and quantities have to be worked out."
The Economic Times said on Wednesday that the government was considering importing one million tonnes of wheat to increase domestic supplies and check rising prices.
The government was expected to make a statement on the floor of parliament on Thursday regarding wheat. Prices have risen dramatically in recent weeks, stirring calls for government intervention.
Earlier analysts and traders had said there was a good chance India would import wheat, but perhaps not as much as one million tonnes.
"One million tonnes is very high. It may not be possible. Maybe imports could be 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes," Tarun Kumar of Space Group, a leading Delhi-based foodgrain trader, said on Wednesday.
In Washington, U.S. Wheat Associates research and marketing analyst Gregg Doud said on Wednesday that India may need to import one million tonnes of wheat in the coming months.
